idiom_name: candidate state + use-named validation gate + violation collector
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: let the object hold whatever has been ingested, missing and suspect values included, and give it one validation operation per anticipated use (validateForSave, validateForPublication) instead of checks in constructors or setters. Each operation delegates to simpler operations and runs the checks in passes - required values present first, then their consistency, then cross-record rules - adding violations to a collector rather than failing on the first problem. Only the action boundary (persist, publish, send) must call the matching operation, and it does so before the irreversible step. Memoise a verdict only together with a version stamp that mutation invalidates.
code_sketch:
candidate = ingest(raw)                        # no checks here
...
if not candidate.validate_for(use, errors):   # gate at the action boundary
    return errors                             # all violations, not the first
commit(candidate)                             # irreversible step only after the gate
pitfalls: A gate that lives only in documentation: if the action does not call the matching validation operation, the deferral becomes missing validation.
Collecting violations and then discarding them at the boundary, so the user sees a generic failure instead of the reasons.
Caching a valid verdict without invalidating it on mutation, so the next action reads a stale judgement.
Omitting the gate before an irreversible effect: validating after commit/publish/post only postpones the damage.

Using deferred validation as a substitute for type-level correctness: when the domain model could use sum types or smart constructors to make illegal states unrepresentable, deferring runtime checks trades compile-time safety for runtime flexibility.

Cascading validation across large object graphs without fail-fast or group sequencing: Hibernate Validator's cascading validation can trigger expensive cycle detection on large aggregates, making the gate expensive on hot paths.

Wrong move: trusting the ORM or serializer to validate on save -> Django's model.save() never calls full_clean(), so rows with constraint-violating or missing values reach the database -> instead call full_clean()/is_valid() explicitly at the action boundary as the gate.

Wrong move: letting Hibernate's pre-insert/pre-update Bean Validation be the only gate -> the violation surfaces as ConstraintViolationException wrapped in RollbackException at commit, far from the mutation that caused it, and the session is usually discarded -> instead run the use-named validation operation before the unit of work opens and keep the lifecycle listener as a backstop.

Wrong move: making every object carry invalid state because a documented bypass exists (save(validate: false)) -> every downstream consumer must re-check and one forgotten gate publishes garbage, the invalid-object anti-pattern -> instead enforce core invariants at construction and defer only the contextual rules.
